name: Multiples — Multiple Orgasms
summary: After orgasm, most clits become super-sensitive—touch that felt good before can now hurt. This oversensitivity makes many women assume multiples aren't possible, but they often are if you treat the post-orgasm body as 'completely different' with new sensitivities and preferences.
detailed_description: OMGYES groups paths to multiples into approaches that work around post-orgasm oversensitivity. About 47% who experience multiples treat the body as brand new and rediscover what works; about 53% use recovery-period methods (rewinding to warmup touch, or a still palm hug) before rebuilding. A lucky ~14% (one in seven) can have immediate multiples—either pushing through with the same motion or switching to fast indirect layering. Building a second orgasm usually means starting from what caused the first and modifying it: less direct touch, slower, lighter, fewer touches on the exposed clit. Most women cannot reach multiples, and that's normal—best treated as a zero-pressure experiment, often discovered through masturbation first.
stepwise_structure: 1. Expect post-orgasm oversensitivity—direct clit touch may hurt right after.
2. Choose an approach: treat the body as new, use a recovery-period method, or (if you're among the lucky ~14%) go for immediate multiples.
3. Protect the oversensitive clit—use lighter, slower, more indirect touch or hold still.
4. Rebuild from what worked for the first orgasm, modified to be gentler.
5. Keep it pressure-free; stop if it's uncomfortable or not happening.
safety_notes: Honor post-orgasm oversensitivity—pushing painful touch is counterproductive.
Most women can't reach multiples; pressuring a partner causes hurt feelings and disappointment.
Approach as a fun, zero-pressure experiment; many discover their pathway via masturbation first.
